page: Amazon Web Services m6gd.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by an ARMv8 AWS Graviton Neoverse-N1 processor. The instance provides 4 dedicated physical cores running at 2.5 GHz with a single thread per core topology. It is provisioned with 16.0 GB of system memory, matching the standard 1:4 core-to-memory ratio characteristic of general-purpose instances, and incorporates 237 GB of direct-attached local NVMe SSD storage alongside a 1 Gbps baseline network interface. The instance does not feature graphics processing units or hardware accelerators.

Benchmark results demonstrate dependable mid-tier performance across synthetic multi-core and memory evaluations. The instance achieved 1520.19 on single-core stress-ng tests and 6055.75 on multi-core stress-ng tests, placing it in the middle tier. Uncached memory bandwidth scored 63.9 GB/sec for reads and 30.56 GB/sec for writes, while PassMark database operations reached an average result of 2648.72. In contrast, complex calculation tests such as Geekbench single-core (921.0), PassMark CPU score (2692.37), and compression benchmarks registered in lower performance quartiles, reflecting the lower clock speed and instruction characteristics of early-generation ARM cloud processors.

The presence of bundled local NVMe storage offers notable cost efficiency for I/O-intensive temporary operations by eliminating network disk round-trips without supplemental storage fees. Amazon Web Services m6gd.xlarge is well balanced for containerized microservices, distributed caching nodes, batch processing, static web serving, and continuous integration workloads that leverage local scratch storage.
description: Amazon Web Services m6gd.xlarge is a general-purpose Nitro-based virtual server powered by a 4-core AWS Graviton Neoverse-N1 ARMv8 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. The configuration allocates 16.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, combined with 237 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD instance storage and 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Synthetic benchmarks show steady mid-range throughput in stress-ng evaluations and PassMark database operations, accompanied by 63.9 GB/sec uncached memory read bandwidth. Although raw single-threaded compute and compression metrics trend lower than high-frequency x86 architectures, the inclusion of dedicated physical cores and integrated local NVMe storage delivers strong resource efficiency. This makes the instance suitable for web servers, containerized workloads, distributed cache nodes, and data processing tasks requiring fast ephemeral storage.
